prerequisites: Basic knowledge of Technical Informatics, including the structure of microprocessors

learning_outcomes.text: Students who have successfully studied this module will have a broad knowledge of modern computer architecture concepts.
After completing this module, students will have acquired in-depth knowledge of powerful microprocessors and their use in parallel computers.
After completing the module, students can evaluate the structure and performance of different computer architectures and select suitable architectures for a given application area.

Upon completion of the module, students can understand existing computer architectures and explain their functionality. They can extract new aspects from scientific technical texts and present and discuss them in a structured and clear manner (e.g., in the form of a presentation).

syllabus_topics: Selected aspects of modern parallel computers (student presentations)
assessment_rules: Normally, the examination format is a presentation. Only if this is not possible due to a high number of participants, the lecture will be held throughout the semester and an exam will be conducted. The presentation duration is approximately 30 minutes with an accompanying elaboration of approximately 8 pages. Exam duration is according to the study regulations.
